transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

My sleep has gotten completely off track. At first I was only sleeping two or three hours, then getting up and making plans, feeling ready to go. Now I’m awake before dawn, just lying there with my stomach tight, and I don’t feel rested at all.
During that time when you were only sleeping two or three hours but felt ready to go, did you notice your mood being unusually high, your energy way up, or your thoughts racing more than usual?

Yes. For weeks I felt almost brilliantly optimistic, like every obstacle was minor and I could handle anything. But if somebody questioned me, I’d snap at them—I felt like they were trying to undermine the only person who was making any sense.
How long did that period of feeling unusually optimistic and full of energy last—was it a few days, or closer to a week or more?
It was much longer than a week—about five months after the investment loss. I wasn’t living like my usual retired self; everything was focused on trying to undo the damage.

Right now, are you having trouble doing your usual daily activities—like managing your routine or taking care of yourself—and have you noticed any unusual experiences, like hearing things others don't or feeling like people are out to harm you?
Yes. My wife has had to take over the finances and stay with me because she’s worried about my safety. And I’ve stopped showing up reliably for the museum, the arts council, even with friends.

During this current low period, have you experienced any false beliefs—like feeling you're being punished or that something terrible is about to happen—or heard or seen things that others don't perceive?
No, I haven’t heard or seen things that other people don’t. I don’t think I have any fixed beliefs like that either.
